subject: biology

moments.title: Hill reaction
moments.body: Hill shows isolated chloroplasts can produce oxygen and reduce non-natural electron acceptors. The light reactions are separable from carbon fixation.
moments.takeaway: Photosynthesis splits into light and dark reactions.

moments.title: Z-scheme
moments.body: Hill and Bendall propose the Z-scheme: two photosystems in series, with electrons pumped up the energy ladder by two photon absorptions. The scheme remains correct.
moments.takeaway: Two photons per electron, in series.

moments.title: PSII crystal structure
moments.body: The 1.9 Å structure of photosystem II reveals the water-oxidising Mn4CaO5 cluster — the most catalytic centre on Earth, splitting water at neutral pH and room temperature.
moments.takeaway: The most important catalytic cluster on Earth is finally seen at atomic resolution.

moments.title: Artificial photosynthesis
moments.body: Solar-fuel research aims to mimic the water-splitting half of PSII with metal-oxide catalysts. Some prototypes reach 10%+ solar-to-hydrogen efficiency.
moments.takeaway: Artificial leaves are being engineered, atom by atom.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Photosynthesis fixes ~120 GtC/year. Crop yield gains from photosynthesis engineering (Rubisco, NPQ relaxation) are showing up in field trials.
now.open_questions: Can we engineer C3 crops with C4 efficiency? Can artificial photosynthesis become competitive with PV+electrolysis?

reflection: PSII performs reaction industrial chemistry can't yet match. Why is biology so far ahead of materials science here?
